conclusion.original: For every parameter probability and ambient weight, the literal potential cross integrand is integrable and HasGradientAt holds for its actual Mathlib gradient. On unit weights G is tangent and uniformly bounded by C₁. For every probability pair, Q<∞ and ‖G_μ(w)-G_ν(u)‖≤C₂(sqrt(Q)+arccos(inner(w,u))). The square root is the real value of the extended square root after finiteness. No optimal coupling or intrinsic geometric identification is asserted.
conclusion.reconstructed: There exist C1,C2:R with C1>0 and C2>0, uniform for all subsequent laws and unit weights. For every probability mu on S, and every ambient w:E, the scalar function z->(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under P, and HasGradientAt(V(mu,.),grad(mu,w),w) holds. For every such probability mu and every w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and, for all w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). Exact definitions and their totalizations: Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1} with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and denote the ambient representative of w:S by w_bar. For every mu:Measure S and x:E define predictor(mu,x)=integral_S p.eval(inner_product_E(w_bar,x)) dmu(w). Define V(mu,w)=2*integral_{E times R}(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) dP(z), for every ambient w:E. Define grad(mu,w)=gradient(V(mu,.),w), the actual Mathlib full ambient gradient, and G(mu,w)=grad(mu,w)-inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),w) times w. Define c(w,u)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)) on S times S. Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over actual measures gamma whose first marginal is mu and second marginal is nu. The empty feasible infimum is infinity; no optimizer is selected or asserted. All predictor and potential integrals are actual real Bochner integrals, totalized to zero if their integrands fail to be integrable. The gradient definition is totalized at points without the corresponding Frechet derivative.

scopes.original: The predictor and scalar potential are literal Bochner integrals. Their analytic properties are proved for probability parameter laws, despite total definitions existing for all measures. Gradient differentiability is full ambient pointwise differentiability with μ fixed. A.e. class identities are used only as intermediate bridges; final scalar function/gradient assertions are pointwise in ambient weights. Projection and estimates are for unit points. If S is empty, probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous. This is a quantitative continuity/boundedness result, not a convergence theorem.
scopes.reconstructed: The Gaussian is the actual first marginal of the fixed joint law P, without an independent response replacement. For each probability mu the scalar cross-term integrability and ambient gradient are asserted for every w:E, including nonunit points; the only scalar function being differentiated is the explicit V(mu,.), with mu fixed. HasGradientAt certifies the actual Frechet derivative represented by the actual grad value, so under these conditions it does not rely on nondifferentiable totalization. G is a true orthogonal tangent projection only for norm(w)=1, and the orthogonality, norm bound, and final comparison are restricted to those subtype points. The definitions are syntactically available for all measures via totalized integrals and gradients, but no analytic conclusion is extended beyond their probability premises. The explicit Integrable clause concerns exactly the displayed joint cross integrand. Q is the nonnegative extended infimum of lower integrals over ordered-marginal couplings, not a signed measure operation. Q finiteness is explicit and prevents interpreting an infinite transport root by toReal=0. No optimizer or new metric/geodesic API conclusion is included. All parameter probabilities, including nonatomic ones, are covered. No law-variable derivative is asserted. Empty S is allowed, making the probability-conditioned assertions vacuous.
